title: Array.get() still prints "Index out of bounds" error to console
body:
### Tested versions

v4.6.stable.official [89cea1439]

### System information

Godot v4.6.stable - Windows 10 (build 19045) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Direct3D 12 (Forward+) - dedicated AMD Radeon RX 6600 XT (Advanced Micro Devices, Inc.; 32.0.21030.2001) - AMD Ryzen 5 5600G with Radeon Graphics (12 threads) - 31.79 GiB memory

### Issue description

I am using the `Array.get()` method to safely read elements from an array when the index might be invalid. The method successfully prevents the game from crashing and returns null as expected, which is great.

However, it still forcefully prints index out of bounds error to the Debugger console every single time the index doesn't exist.
This completely defeats the purpose of using `get()`. It creates a huge amount of error spam in my logs during loops or gameplay logic. `Dictionary.get()` works perfectly and silently returns null if a key is missing. `Array.get()` should do the same and not spam the console with red errors if the developer explicitly chose to use a safe getter method.

Error message:
```gd
E 0:00:03:501   hire_menu.gd:77 @ _on_hire_btn_pressed(): Index p_index = 0 is out of bounds (p_instance->size() = 0).
  <C++ Source>  core/variant/variant_call.cpp:681 @ func_Array_get()
  <Stack Trace> hire_menu.gd:77 @ _on_hire_btn_pressed()
```

### Steps to reproduce

Run this code in any script:
```gd
var my_array = ["A", "B"]
var item = my_array.get(5) # This shouldn't spam into debugger, but it does.
```

N/A
